affected_system: pedestrian right-of-way, crossings, sidewalks, and accessible routes
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources
pair minimum-access and severity-constrained crew allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Crash, conflict, barrier, sidewalk, crossing, and demand data have explicit observation processes.
Accessibility is evaluated across route continuity, slope, surface, crossing, and obstruction dimensions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources.

constraints.description: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: vision-zero director and accessibility compliance officer
decision_question: How should inspectors, temporary barriers, signal crews, and accessibility repairs be distributed?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The pedestrian safety and universal accessibility allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.primary_outcome: verified high-consequence barriers without assigned response

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: verified high-consequence barriers without assigned response
distributional gap in verified high-consequence barriers without assigned response
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned crews as completed repairs or verified compliance.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for pedestrian inspection and quick-build resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate inspections and quick-build safety resources
transportability_risks: Street design, enforcement, mobility-device needs, exposure, and reporting vary by place.
Crash-only models underrepresent near misses and unreported accessibility barriers.
